ov: Small, spiny insect-eaters of Europe, Asia and Africa that roll into a tight ball when threatened. There are 17 species; the European hedgehog is the familiar garden one.

why.d: Mostly insects, worms and slugs, which is why gardeners like having them around.
why.h: All wild hedgehogs can hibernate. Body temperature drops from about 30–35 °C to as low as 2–5 °C.
why.p: The pet kind is mostly the African pygmy hedgehog. Keeping a wild hedgehog is illegal in some countries, such as France and Italy.
why.et: Eaten in ancient Egypt and medieval Europe, and still eaten by some Romani communities.
why.ac: Largely nocturnal, snuffling along and stopping often to smell the air.

rg: Europe, Asia and Africa; none native to the Americas or Australia. The European hedgehog was introduced to New Zealand, where it is now a pest.
df: Insects, worms, slugs and snails, plus eggs, carrion and fallen fruit.
fx: The European hedgehog is now listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.
notes: Group entry (17 species); no species pages to link. ADW gives a length of 135–165 mm, which looks low against Wikipedia's "260 mm or more in large adults", so I used Wikipedia. df "eggs, carrion and fallen fruit": check the European hedgehog Diet section.
